mergedParams.userDescription: Ultra-thin, lightweight text drifting downwards slowly like ash. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Ash-Like Drifting Text - Lightweight Typokinetic Animation

prompts.prompt: Create a typography preset that simulates text particles drifting downward like volcanic ash falling through still air. From a video editor's perspective, imagine each word or letter as a separate layer with unique drift patterns - some falling straight, others caught in subtle air currents. The text should start with minimal opacity (10-20%) and gradually become more visible as it descends, like ash becoming denser. Use TextAtom components within BaseLayout containers, each with individual transform animations. Apply a slight gaussian blur that decreases as text falls (simulating focus pull). Include random horizontal drift using translateX with sine-wave easing for natural movement. The overall effect should feel meditative and weightless, perfect for titles that need to convey fragility or transience.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Main BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' containing multiple nested BaseLayouts for each text element. Each word gets its own BaseLayout with 'absolute' positioning and staggered start times. Use TextAtom with initial opacity:0.1 and blur(8px). Create generic keyframe effects with AnimationRange arrays: translateY from -20% to 120% over full duration, translateX using Math.sin() for drift (-5% to 5%), opacity from 0.1 to 0.8 to 0.3, blur from 8px to 0px. Use 'ease-in' easing for gravity feel. Set transform-style: preserve-3d and will-change: transform, opacity for GPU optimization. Implement random delays (0-2s) for each word's animation start. Consider fitDurationTo: 'self' with minimum 8 seconds for proper pacing.

prompts.prompt: Design a kinetic typography preset where ultra-thin text dissolves and reforms like particles in a dust storm. Think of this as a video effect where text breaks apart into individual pixels or dots that drift downward while maintaining loose cohesion. From an editor's timeline view, you'd see opacity keyframes pulsing between 20-60% while position keyframes create chaotic but controlled movement. The text should feel ephemeral - barely there but readable. Use letter-spacing animations to simulate dispersion, and implement a subtle turbulence effect using multiple overlapping sine waves for x-axis movement. This creates the illusion of text being carried by invisible air currents.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use caption-based typography with word-level timing. Main BaseLayout with 'flex flex-col items-center justify-center w-full h-full'. For each word from caption data, create BaseLayout with 'relative inline-block mx-1'. Apply TextAtom with font 'Inter:100:normal' and initial 'text-white/20'. Implement custom effects array: letterSpacing animating from 0 to 0.3em, opacity oscillating 0.2 to 0.6 using multiple keyframes, translateY 0 to 100vh over duration. Add translateX using composite sine waves (Math.sin(time*2) * 10 + Math.sin(time*3) * 5) for turbulence. Use mix-blend-mode: screen for ethereal quality. Apply CSS filter: contrast(1.2) brightness(0.8) for dusty appearance. Stagger animations based on word.relativeStart from caption data.

prompts.prompt: Construct a minimalist ash-fall typography effect where text appears to be written in falling cinders. Visualize this as a high-end title sequence where each character materializes from drifting particles that coalesce briefly before continuing their descent. From a motion graphics perspective, use particle physics - initial burst velocity, gravity acceleration, and air resistance. Text should fade in as particles converge, remain legible for a beat, then disperse downward. Include subtle heat shimmer using SVG filters or CSS transforms. The aesthetic should evoke the quiet aftermath of destruction - beautiful but melancholic.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with scene-type preset containing sequential BaseLayouts. Each BaseLayout represents a text phase: convergence, display, dispersion. Use TextAtom with 'font-extralight tracking-widest text-gray-300'. Implement three-stage effect system: Stage 1 (0-30%): particles converge using radial translateX/Y from random positions, opacity 0 to 0.9. Stage 2 (30-70%): hold position with subtle vibration (translateX: Math.random()*2-1), maintain opacity. Stage 3 (70-100%): disperse with translateY accelerating (ease-in), translateX diverging, opacity to 0. Add SVG turbulence filter for heat shimmer: <feTurbulence baseFrequency='0.02' numOctaves='2'/>. Use transform: translate3d() for hardware acceleration. Consider sub-preset for reusable particle behavior.

prompts.prompt: Develop a cinematic text drift effect inspired by film noir title cards where words emerge from darkness and float downward like smoke wisps. Picture editing this in Premiere - you'd use blend modes, feathered masks, and subtle distortion. Text should have varying weights within the same word (first letters heavier, trailing letters lighter) creating a gradient effect. Implement film grain texture and slight chromatic aberration for authenticity. Movement should be hypnotically slow with micro-movements suggesting air currents. Perfect for atmospheric titles in dramatic content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'bg-black w-full h-full relative' containing gradient overlay 'absolute inset-0 bg-gradient-to-b from-transparent via-black/50 to-black'. For typography, parse caption data and create TextAtom for each word with variable font weight using CSS font-variation-settings. Apply 'mix-blend-mode: difference' or 'exclusion' for noir aesthetic. Create multi-layered effects: primary drift (translateY: 0 to 80vh over 10s, ease-out), micro-drift (translateX: sine wave amplitude 2px, period 3s), rotation (rotate: -1deg to 1deg, ease-in-out). Add CSS filter chain: contrast(1.1) brightness(0.95) blur(0.3px) for film look. Implement ::before pseudo-element with grain texture using CSS background-image with noise pattern. Use text-shadow for chromatic aberration: '1px 1px 0 rgba(255,0,0,0.3), -1px -1px 0 rgba(0,0,255,0.3)'.

prompts.prompt: Create an ethereal floating text preset where typography behaves like weightless particles in zero gravity before being pulled downward. Think of After Effects' particle world - text elements spawn with random velocities, float momentarily, then succumb to increasing gravity. From an editor's view, velocity curves would show exponential acceleration. Text should shimmer with iridescence using animated gradients. Include parallax layers with different fall speeds for depth. This style suits dream sequences or surreal content where reality feels suspended.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Implement physics-based animation using presetExecution calculations. Main BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full perspective-1000' for 3D space. Create three depth layers using z-index and scale. For each caption word, calculate: initialVelocity = {x: Math.random()*4-2, y: Math.random()*2-3}, gravity = 0.98. Update position each frame: velocity.y *= gravity, position += velocity. Convert to CSS transforms. TextAtom with animated gradient background: 'bg-gradient-to-r from-purple-400/30 via-pink-400/30 to-blue-400/30 bg-clip-text text-transparent'. Animate gradient position using backgroundPosition. Apply transform: translateZ() for parallax layers (near: 100px, mid: 0px, far: -100px) with corresponding scale adjustments. Use requestAnimationFrame timing via effects system with 60fps keyframes. Include subtle rotateX/Y for tumbling effect.

prompts.prompt: Design a poetic ash-rain typography where text appears handwritten by falling embers, each letter materializing as particles land and cool. Imagine editing a sequence where glowing particles trace letterforms before dimming to ash-gray. From a VFX perspective, combine particle emission with text reveal masks. Letters should appear sequentially with ember glow that fades to matte gray. Include wind gusts that temporarily scatter particles sideways. The mood should be elegiac - beautiful destruction, like words written in the aftermath of fire.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use dependencies to import particle-system helper. Structure with BaseLayout 'bg-gradient-to-b from-gray-900 to-black w-full h-full'. For each letter in caption text, create timed reveal sequence. Initial state: TextAtom with 'opacity-0 text-transparent'. Reveal animation: clipPath progressing from 'inset(100% 0 0 0)' to 'inset(0 0 0 0)' synchronized with particle landing. Particle system: generate 3-5 particles per letter using absolute positioned divs with 'w-1 h-1 rounded-full'. Particle effects: initial color 'bg-orange-500' with glow 'shadow-[0_0_10px_rgba(251,146,60,0.8)]', transition to 'bg-gray-500' over 2s. Movement: translateY from -50px to letter position + 100px, translateX using wind function Math.sin(time*windSpeed)*windStrength. Letter glow effect: text-shadow transitioning from '0 0 20px rgba(251,146,60,0.9)' to '0 0 0 transparent'. Stagger each letter reveal by 0.2s using word.relativeStart + letterIndex*0.2.

prompts.prompt: Build a documentary-style lower-third preset where text drifts down like archival typewriter text on aged paper. Picture Ken Burns effect meets falling autumn leaves - text should feel weathered, with slight rotation and varying speeds suggesting different 'weights' of paper. From an editorial standpoint, this conveys history and gravitas. Include paper texture, typewriter font, and subtle sepia toning. Text opacity should vary like old ink - some letters darker, others faded. Perfect for historical documentaries or nostalgic content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-gradient-to-br from-amber-50/10 to-yellow-50/10'. Apply paper texture using CSS background-image with multiply blend mode. Use 'Courier Prime:400:normal' or 'Special Elite:400:normal' font. For each word, create BaseLayout with 'absolute' positioning and random initial top position (-10% to -30%). Implement gravity simulation with air resistance: acceleration decreases over time using easing: 'cubic-bezier(0.55, 0.085, 0.68, 0.53)'. Add rotation: random initial rotation (-15deg to 15deg), slight rotation during fall (0.5deg/s). Vary opacity per character using inline styles: opacity: 0.4 + Math.random()*0.6. Apply sepia filter: 'sepia(0.3) contrast(0.95) brightness(1.05)'. Include paper flutter effect: translateX oscillating with sine wave (amplitude: 10px, frequency based on 'weight'). Use transform-origin: 'center center' for natural rotation. Consider fitDurationTo: 'children' to ensure all text completes animation.

prompts.prompt: Craft a modern glitch-ash hybrid where digital text breaks apart into pixels that fall like digital snow. Think datamoshing meets particle systems - text corrupts into blocks that cascade downward with digital artifacts. From a post-production view, combine displacement maps with particle physics. Text should glitch between readable and corrupted states while descending. Include RGB split effects, scan lines, and digital noise. This style works for cyberpunk aesthetics or tech-focused content where decay meets digital.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Main BaseLayout 'bg-black w-full h-full overflow-hidden relative'. Implement glitch effect using multiple TextAtom layers with different blend modes. Base layer: normal text. Glitch layers: duplicate with 'mix-blend-mode: screen' and RGB channel offsets using CSS filters. Create glitch keyframes: random intervals where text splits into blocks using clip-path rectangles. Each block gets independent physics: mass = blockSize, gravityMultiplier = mass/100. Apply transform: translate3d() for block movement. RGB split: use text-shadow with red/cyan offsets '2px 2px 0 rgba(255,0,0,0.5), -2px -2px 0 rgba(0,255,255,0.5)'. Digital artifacts: add ::after pseudo-element with animated linear-gradient creating scan lines. Noise: CSS background with base64 encoded noise pattern, animated opacity 0.1 to 0.3. Glitch timing: use step() easing for instant transitions. Include data corruption effect: randomly replace characters with Unicode blocks '█▓▒░'. Performance: use CSS containment 'contain: layout style paint'.

prompts.prompt: Develop a liquid text preset where words melt and drip downward like wax or heavy oil. Visualize editing a high-speed footage reverse - text maintains form briefly then liquefies, stretching vertically as it falls. From a motion design angle, use morphing techniques with SVG filters for realistic liquid distortion. Text should have weight and viscosity - thick parts fall faster, thin parts stretch. Include surface tension effects where letters briefly resist separation. Suitable for horror titles or artistic projects requiring organic, unsettling movement.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use SVG filters for liquid distortion. BaseLayout with filter container: '<svg><defs><filter id="liquid"><feTurbulence baseFrequency="0.015" /><feDisplacementMap scale="20" /></filter></defs></svg>'. Apply filter to TextAtom via style prop: {filter: 'url(#liquid)'}. Implement multi-phase animation: Phase 1 (0-40%): stable with micro-vibrations. Phase 2 (40-70%): vertical stretch using scaleY (1 to 1.5) and translateY beginning. Phase 3 (70-100%): accelerate fall with scaleY continuing to 3, opacity fading. Use font with heavy weight 'Oswald:700:normal' for better distortion visibility. Add custom path animation for drips: create absolutely positioned divs below letters, animate height from 0 to random value, use border-radius for drop shape. Viscosity simulation: heavier parts (capitals, bold) fall faster using weight-based gravity multiplier. Surface tension: slight elastic bounce using spring easing before final fall. Include gooey effect: filter blur(0.5px) combined with contrast(20) then blur(0.5px) again.

prompts.prompt: Create a time-lapse photography effect where text ages and crumbles while falling like ancient inscriptions turning to dust. Picture documentary footage of weathering stone - text starts crisp, develops cracks, fragments, then falls as powder. From a cinematography perspective, simulate decades passing in seconds. Include erosion patterns, color bleaching, and fragment physics. Each piece should fall at different rates based on size. Perfect for epic historical narratives or themes of impermanence and time's passage.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Implement fragment system using caption data split into individual characters. Each character becomes a BaseLayout with 'relative inline-block' containing multiple fragment divs. Initial TextAtom state: 'text-stone-600 font-serif font-bold'. Erosion sequence: Stage 1: Add crack overlay using CSS linear-gradients as masks. Stage 2: Split into fragments using clip-path polygons (3-5 per letter). Stage 3: Apply physics to fragments - smaller pieces have air resistance, larger pieces fall faster. Fragment generation: use Voronoi-like pattern or predefined crack templates. Animation timeline: 0-30%: aging (color shifts from text-stone-600 to text-stone-400, subtle texture via multiple text-shadows). 30-60%: cracking (clip-path animations revealing splits, slight fragment separation). 60-100%: falling (each fragment gets unique translateY/X and rotate based on size/mass). Use CSS custom properties for fragment physics: --mass, --air-resistance, --spin. Apply filter: brightness() and contrast() for weathering. Consider creating internal effect preset 'stone-crumble' for reusability. Performance: use transform: translateZ(0) for layer promotion.
